main_body: traditional Japanese two-story building (machiya) with tiled roof and lattice facade
top_band: grey-blue tiled upper roof slope from rows 1 to 30 (and secondary roof awning at rows 41 to 46)
evidence: The upper roof slope (rows 1-30) and the secondary awning roof (rows 41-46) are clearly visible from above with foreshortened tile rows, distinct front-edge eaves (rows 29-30, 45-46), eave shadows beneath them (rows 31-32, 47), and recessed upper windows (rows 34-39) and doorway (rows 51-76) on the vertical south facade.

style.evidence: The candidate matches the Beodeul reference standard closely: the kawara roof tiles use 6 distinct grey-blue lightness steps with per-tile highlights, the plaster wall has subtle brick/speckle grain, the wooden lattice and bamboo fenders have rich multi-step shading, and outlines are dark material tones rather than flat black.
